chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to issue fatwas during the era of the Banu Umayya that whatever the falcon and the hawk kills is permissible, and he was observing dissimulation (taqiyya) from them. But I do not fear them, and it is forbidden — what they kill.'

key_terms.الصَّقْرُ: The hawk/saqr — another bird of prey used in hunting
key_terms.الْبَازِي: The falcon (al-Bazi) — a bird of prey used in falconry
key_terms.يَتَّقِيهِمْ: Taqiyya (dissimulation) — concealing true beliefs or issuing expedient rulings under threat
key_terms.يُفْتِي: To issue a fatwa — a religious legal opinion

ai.seo_question: Is the prey of falcons and hawks halal or haram in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reveals that his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS), had issued a fatwa permitting the consumption of prey killed by falcons and hawks during the oppressive Umayyad era, but this ruling was given under taqiyya (religious dissimulation) for self-preservation. Now that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) is no longer under the same political duress, he declares the authentic ruling: such prey is actually forbidden (haram). This hadith is a significant example of how taqiyya affected jurisprudential pronouncements, demonstrating that the Imams sometimes issued temporary rulings that differed from the true hukm due to political circumstances.
